callout.title: Safe Parsing Pattern
callout.text: Always use int.TryParse or double.TryParse when reading from the console to avoid uncaught FormatException crashes.

checkpoint.question: What is the primary advantage of int.TryParse over int.Parse when processing user input?
options: It returns a boolean indicating success and does not throw an exception on invalid format
It can parse floating-point numbers directly into integers
It reads directly from disk files instead of console
checkpoint.explanation: int.TryParse returns false if parsing fails instead of throwing a costly FormatException, making it robust against bad user input.

questions.question: What data type does Console.ReadLine() return in C#?
options: string (or string? in nullable reference types)
questions.explanation: Console.ReadLine() reads the next line of characters from the standard input stream and returns it as a string.

questions.question: What exception is thrown by int.Parse("abc")?
questions.explanation: When the input string does not contain a recognizable integer representation, int.Parse throws a System.FormatException.

questions.question: How does Convert.ToInt32(null) behave compared to int.Parse(null)?
options: Convert.ToInt32(null) returns 0, while int.Parse(null) throws ArgumentNullException
questions.explanation: Convert.ToInt32 handles null arguments by returning 0, whereas int.Parse throws an ArgumentNullException.

questions.question: What method reads a single key press from the user without requiring them to press Enter?
questions.explanation: Console.ReadKey() intercepts the next key pressed by the user and returns a ConsoleKeyInfo object without waiting for Enter.

questions.question: If user inputs multiple space-separated numbers on one line, how can you parse them into an array of integers?
questions.explanation: Splitting the line with .Split(' ') and converting each element via Array.ConvertAll(..., int.Parse) or LINQ .Select(int.Parse) is the standard idiomatic technique.

questions.question: What does the `out` parameter in `int.TryParse(input, out int result)` signify?
options: It passes the variable by reference as an output target for the parsed result
It marks the variable as obsolete
It writes the variable directly to standard output
questions.explanation: The out modifier passes an argument by reference, requiring the callee method to assign a value to it before returning.

questions.question: Which property changes the text color displayed in the console window in C#?
questions.explanation: Console.ForegroundColor sets the ConsoleColor used for foreground text printed to standard output.

questions.question: Which method clears the console buffer and display area?
questions.explanation: Console.Clear() clears the console buffer and corresponding display window.

questions.question: What does Console.Read() return when reading from standard input?
options: The integer ASCII/Unicode value of the next character, or -1 if no more characters are available
questions.explanation: Console.Read() reads the next character from the input stream and returns its integer representation, or -1 at EOF.

questions.question: Which stream is used to print error diagnostic messages in C#?
questions.explanation: Console.Error represents the standard error output stream, allowing errors to be routed separately from standard output.
